details:
Q1: The poller's four review-run matchers on current `main` don't check `head_branch == <default branch>`. `_pr_named_review_dispatch_runs` doesn't even ask GitHub for `head_branch`, and there's no default-branch cache to reuse. Should this issue harden them too?
Choices:
A) Yes. Harden the merge train, the sweep and the four poller matchers. Add one default-branch read per poller tick (or reuse an existing repo-metadata read) and fail closed with a warning when it can't be resolved. `_autofix_pr_named_review_runs` already complies and only gets spoof tests. (RECOMMENDED)
B) No. Harden only `_mt_inflight_review_branches` and the sweep's `dispatch_pr` matcher, plus spoof tests for `_autofix_pr_named_review_runs`. File a separate issue for the poller.
C) Harden only the poller's four matchers here, and file the merge train and sweep as a follow-up.
Q2: GitHub can report `head_branch: null` on a real default-branch `workflow_dispatch` review run (issue #4928). The sweep keeps such runs by their `pr:<N>` title on purpose, because dropping them let the next tick dispatch again and replace the pending review. How should every hardened matcher treat a null `head_branch`?
Choices:
A) Accept `head_branch` equal to the resolved default branch **or** null/empty, but only if `event == workflow_dispatch` and the exact title matches its own wrapper path. Reject any other non-empty branch. This keeps the #4928 fix and still rejects a branch-copy spoof. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Strict: require `head_branch` to equal the default branch and drop null runs. This reverts the #4928 protection, so the sweep may dispatch duplicates again.
C) Strict match, but a null `head_branch` makes the listing "incomplete". Each caller then uses its existing fail-closed path (skip dispatch or hold release this tick).
Q3: In `_mt_inflight_review_branches`, any review-path `workflow_dispatch` run without a PR-named title currently marks the whole listing `unattributed_run` and holds every merge-train release. After hardening, what happens to a review-wrapper dispatch run on a non-default branch, or one whose title and path don't pair?
Choices:
A) Ignore it: it's not a trusted review run, so it neither keys a PR nor holds the train. Keep today's `unattributed_run` handling for default-branch dispatches without a PR title, such as `review_autofix.yml` self-dispatches. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Keep treating it as `unattributed_run`, which marks the listing incomplete and holds every release this tick. That keeps the availability stall the issue is trying to remove.
